items.scenario: An email from "Hana (CEO)" asks you to pay a supplier today. It comes from an address you have not seen before.
items.stem: Which detail is a warning sign under the payment policy?

options.text: The sender address doesn't match the usual one
options.feedback: Right. A sender or reply-to address that does not match the usual one is a listed warning sign.

options.text: The email is addressed to you by name
options.feedback: A personal greeting proves nothing either way; attackers use names too.

options.text: The email is sent during working hours
options.feedback: Timing alone is not a listed sign; look at the address, urgency, bank details and secrecy.

items.explanation: A sender address or reply-to address that does not match the usual one is a warning sign of a fake payment request.

items.scenario: Friday, 4:50 p.m. "Hana (CEO)" emails Sam in Finance: pay a supplier today, use new bank details, keep it quiet.

options.feedback: Seniority is never a reason to skip verification. Unverified payments must not be made.

options.text: Reply to the email to check
options.feedback: A reply goes to the sender of the request. Never use contact details given in the request itself.

options.text: Call Hana on her directory number
options.feedback: Yes. Requests from executives are verified by calling back on their directory number.

items.explanation: A request from an executive is verified by calling the executive back on their directory number or confirming in person; never use contact details from the request.

items.stem: The email lists a new phone number so you can "confirm". What do you do?

options.text: Call the new number in the email
options.feedback: That number belongs to whoever sent the request. Never use contact details given in the request.

options.text: Call a number already on file
options.feedback: Right. Call back on a number already on file in the supplier master or company directory.

options.text: Text the new number for a quick yes
options.feedback: Any channel the request gives you can reach the attacker. Use a number already on file.

items.explanation: Never use a phone number, link or contact detail given in the request itself; call back a number already on file.

items.stem: You think a fake payment request has just been paid. What is the first thing to do?

options.text: Report it to IT Security and Finance immediately
options.feedback: Yes. Fast reporting gives the bank the best chance to stop the transfer.

options.text: Delete the email so it can't spread
options.feedback: Don't delete it: report first, so IT Security can investigate.

options.text: Wait until Monday to be sure
options.feedback: Waiting costs time. Report immediately; fast reporting can stop the transfer.

items.explanation: If you think money has already been sent, report it to IT Security and Finance immediately; fast reporting gives the bank the best chance to stop the transfer.
